lado_card.texto: G0 shows the agentic company and the role of the 2027 manager. The other courses in the program start from it.

rodape: INEMA.CLUB · open and free content · INEMA Learning v7.2 format · eventos.inema.pro/gestao-ia · Horizonte lab (fictional study company) · inema.club

inicio.lead: The vendor shows you what each call costs. The manager needs to know what each result costs. In eight lessons, you calculate the cost per completed task, choose the model based on your own cases, organize the knowledge the agent reads, give the tools the minimum access, find the shadow AI, plan your exit from a vendor, and build a budget and estimated ROI without promising savings.
inicio.capa_alt: A distributor's manager reviews a budget sheet at the end of the day, next to a laptop with a bar chart; in the background, the warehouse shelves.
inicio.aulas_sub: First the math (what the result costs), then each resource that goes into it: the model, the knowledge, the tools, what the team already uses on the side, and the vendor. Lessons 7 and 8 bring it all together in the budget and the area's resource plan.

itens: Area managers, owners of small or mid-sized companies, operations or HR leaders who already have, or soon will have, AI agents on the team.
People who don't code and don't want to: here you manage the agent. Building an agent is a different course.
People who sign off on the agent's invoice, or will have to explain to the owner what it costs and what it returns.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Calculate the cost per completed task, including human time and rework, and not just the price per call.
Choose the model by comparing two configurations on your own cases, with a selection report and an alternative.
Keep the knowledge the agent reads with an owner, a version and an expiry date, and give the tools only the access the task requires.
Build the monthly budget, the estimated ROI in three scenarios and the exit plan for a vendor.

blocos.t: The case that runs through the course
itens: Horizonte Distribuidora, a fictional study company of 40 people that distributes cleaning products in the interior of São Paulo.
You play Patrícia Lima, sales manager, who is responsible for Hora, an agent that sells over WhatsApp. The process is the order that comes in through WhatsApp and goes all the way to invoicing.

The failures planted in the lab (the email assistant that deletes without asking, the tools IT doesn't know about, the dashboard with no baseline) become management problems. Every lesson has one practice on Horizonte and another on your own process.
